verdicts.note: Subspace-labels page: U names a label (a nondegenerate subspace), not the ambient space of the bilinear form. Use another letter for the label, or state here that U is a label.
Subset-intersection page: W is a volume shrink factor, not a subspace as on the bilinear-form page. Use another letter for the shrink factor or for the subspace.
Complex-phase page: a is a kernel scalar, not the integer real numerator part of a Gaussian dyadic. Keep the explicit not-the-numerator-parts statement or use another letter for the kernel scalar.

Complex-phase page: b is a kernel scalar, not the integer imaginary numerator part of a Gaussian dyadic. Keep the explicit not-the-numerator-parts statement or use another letter for the kernel scalar.
Cyclic-convolution page: t is a sequence length, whereas on the radix-digit page t is the polynomial indeterminate. Use another letter (for example n) for the length.
Synthetic-transforms page: a is a vector of records (ring elements), not a sequence of complex numbers. Use another letter for the records or state the change explicitly.
Polynomial-ring page: k is an unbounded power exponent, not an index into the length-t output c. Use another letter (for example e) for the exponent.
Polynomial-ring page: k is a power exponent, not a DFT output index in 0 to q-1. Use another letter (for example e) for the exponent.
Chinese-remainder page: d counts the axes, whereas on the radix-digit page d is the digit width in bits. Use another letter (for example D) for the axis count.
Chinese-remainder page: x is an integer coefficient position, whereas on the DFT page x is an input vector. Use another letter for one of them.
Exact-multiplication page: x is a binary string input, whereas on the Chinese-remainder page x is an integer position. Use another letter for the position (for example p).
Chinese-remainder page: z is a target position, whereas on the exact-multiplication page z is an integer to encode. Use another letter for the target position.
Bluestein page: t is a reduced index in 0 to q-1, not a sequence length. Use another letter for the index or for the length.
Signed-packing page: F is the packed integer f(2^w), not the forward synthetic transform. Use another letter (for example P) for the packed integer.
Signed-packing page: G is the packed integer g(2^w), not the opposite transform. Use another letter (for example Q) for the packed integer.
Bilinear-form page: u is a vector of U, whereas on the butterfly page u is a scalar coefficient of a pair. Use another letter for one of them.
Address-interchange page: u is a field width in bits, whereas on the butterfly page u is a coefficient value. Use another letter for one of them.
Fixed-tape page: u is a cell count per field, whereas on the butterfly page u is a coefficient value. Use another letter for one of them.
Bilinear-form page: v is a vector of U, whereas on the butterfly page v is a scalar coefficient of a pair. Use another letter for one of them.
Bilinear-form page: u is a vector of U, whereas on the guard-width page u is a scalar input coefficient. Use another letter for one of them.
Address-interchange page: u is a field width in bits, whereas on the guard-width page u is a coefficient. Use another letter for one of them.
Fixed-tape page: u is a cell count per field, whereas on the guard-width page u is a coefficient. Use another letter for one of them.
Bilinear-form page: v is a vector of U, whereas on the guard-width page v is a scalar input coefficient. Use another letter for one of them.
Polynomial-ring page: k is a power exponent that is not bounded by the convolution length. Use another letter (for example e) for the exponent, or for the coefficient index on the recovery page.
Gaussian-dyadics page: k is the denominator exponent, whereas on the recovery page k is a coefficient index. Use another letter for one of them.
Discrete-Fourier-transform page: x is an input vector of complex numbers, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page x is an address chunk. Use another letter for the chunk.
Subspace-labels page: x is a vector of F, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page x is an address chunk. Use another letter for the chunk.
Subspace-labels page: y is a vector of F, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page y is an address chunk. Use another letter for the chunk.
Simultaneous-butterfly page: z is a list of stored values, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page z is an address chunk. Use another letter for the chunk.
Tensor-product page: f is a basis vector of Q, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page f is a count of selected positions. Use another letter for the count.
Discrete-Fourier-transform page: i indexes input entries, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page i indexes selected bit positions. Use another letter (for example s) for the selected index.
Cyclic-convolution page: i indexes entries of a, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page i indexes selected bit positions. Use another letter (for example s) for the selected index.
Complex-phase page: i is the imaginary unit, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page i is a selected index. Use another letter (for example s) for the selected index.
Subspace-labels page: R is an orthogonal residual, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page R is a record bit count. Use another letter for the bit count.
Bilinear-form page: B is a bilinear form function, whereas on the packed-bit-addition page B is an exceptional address set. Use another letter for the set.
Discrete-Fourier-transform page: i indexes input entries, whereas on the prime-source-lengths page i is an axis index. Use another letter for the axis index.
Cyclic-convolution page: i indexes entries of a, whereas on the prime-source-lengths page i is an axis index. Use another letter for the axis index.
